# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 26 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 1QHa (Cave 1), Col. 26 | **Condition:** very fragmentary

---

**1** [...] blessed [...] for You gave [...] knowledge to Your servant [...]

**2** [...] so I could understand Your wonders and proclaim [...] the depth of [...]

**3** [...] Your mercy. Blessed are You, Lord, compassionate God [...]

**4** [...] how vast is Your plan and how abundant are Your works [...]

**5** [...] They are magnificent! Blessed are You, Lord, who planted understanding [...]

**6** [...] in the heart of Your servant, so I could see into all these things [...]

**7** [...] and hold back from doing evil, and bless [...]

**8** [...] Your name. For Your delight is in [...] all Your works [...]

**9** [...] and the child of Your servant, You [...] with insight [...]

**10** [...] to stand before You forever [...]

**11** [...] but who is any mortal to understand [...]

**12** [...] what You have done? And how could anyone ever born presume to sit [...]

**13** [...] in Your presence? We are only kneaded from dust, and our end [...]

**14** [...] is to be food for worms. We are spit and molded clay [...]

**15** [...] and our deepest craving is to return to dust. What can clay say back [...]

**16** [...] and what can a handmade thing understand about any plan? [...]

**17** [...] and how could it ever be declared righteous? [...]

**18** [...] As for me, dust that I am, what [...] can I possibly say [...]

**19** [...] and what plans can I make on my own? For [...] when You are angry [...]

**20** [...] Your astonishing [...] mysteries You whispered into the ear of dust [...]

**21** [...] and on the heart of [...] You etched things that last forever [...]

**22** [...] and You unlocked [...] the wellspring of understanding [...]

**23** [...] because there is no [...] truth except what comes from You [...]

**24** [...] and no righteousness outside of Your counsel [...]

**25** [...] and everything [...] lies open before You, and through knowing [...]

**26** [...] Your truth You set everything in place [...]

**27** [...] and nothing happens without Your choosing it [...]

**28** [...] and nothing can be known apart from You [...]

**29** [...] Your astonishing mysteries [...] lasting forever [...]

**30** [...] and ever [...]

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 26 is very fragmentary. The triple blessing formula gives this column a liturgical feel even in its broken state. The "ear of dust" image (26:20) — God whispering secrets into a creature made of dirt — is rendered dynamically as "whispered into the ear of dust" to capture the intimacy of the revelation. The persistent self-abasement (dust, worms, spittle, clay) is the Hodayot's way of magnifying grace: the lower the creature, the greater the gift of knowledge.*
